title: Close every partition writer of an ingest run

blocks.text: An ingest run writes sensor rows into one file per partition of the object store. It opens a partition's writer when the first row for that partition arrives, so the number of writers is known only at run time and they can't be declared in one try-with-resources header. The run itself is the resource: the job does `try (PartitionWriters run = ...)`.

The object store flushes a writer's last rows when it is closed, and that flush can fail. After a night when the store was briefly unavailable, two things were found: partitions whose files were never closed, and an alert that named one failed partition when three had failed.

Write `close()` in `src/main/java/practice/PartitionWriters.java` so the run ends the way it would if every writer had been declared in a try-with-resources header in the order it was opened. About ten lines.

cases.says: closing the run closes each writer it opened
a writer whose close fails does not stop the other writers from being closed, and the failure reaches the caller
the writers are closed in the reverse of the order they were opened
when several writers fail to close, the failure of the first one closed is the exception thrown
the other close failures are attached to the thrown exception as suppressed, none lost

origin.section: A close() Failure Is Attached as Suppressed, Not Thrown in Place of the Body's Exception

concepts: Code that closes several resources itself closes the newest first and keeps closing the others after one fails.
When the body and a close() both throw, the body's exception is thrown and the close failure is attached to it as suppressed, where a close in finally would replace it.
